sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Ajit Kumar,J.
1.

Petitioner is aggrieved by the departmental proceedings which has now come to be instituted against the petitioner by submission of charge-sheet on 28.06.2021.
2.

It is argued on behalf of the petitioner that the charges leveled in the departmental proceedings are same and basis is also the same as has come to be recited in a criminal case arising of Case Crime No.400 of 2020 in which now the charge-sheet has also been submitted by the police under Sections 406 & 420 Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Eastern Coalfields Limited & ors vs. Rabindra Kumar Bharti; 2022 (1) SCC 390 where the departmental proceedings were basically based upon the criminal case, were held to be bad.

entities.text: Eastern Coalfields Limited & ors vs. Rabindra Kumar Bharti; 2022 (1) SCC 390
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The corollary as sought to be drawn by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that department cannot have its own independent witness in respect of the charges which are based upon the criminal proceedings and, therefore, in view of para 492 of UP Police Regulations, departmental proceedings should be stayed.
4. Counsel for the petitioner submits that after submission of charge-sheet, criminal case is at the stage of framing of charges.

5. Per contra, it is argued by the learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel that looking to the departmental charge-sheet that has been brought on record as Annexure-5 to the writ petition, it clearly transpires that there are three independent witnesses to prove the guilt.

Those witnesses have not been taken by the police in its charge-sheet submitted by it against the petitioner before the Court concerned and therefore, he submits that departmental proceedings should not be permitted to be stayed.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and having perused the record, what I find is that the allegations of selling away cars by the fraudulent means or committing forgery, as has come to be leveled in charge-sheet is also basically the charge in the criminal case in which the police has submitted charge-sheet under Sections 406 & 420 Indian Penal Code.
The question as to whether petitioner is involved in such criminal activity so as to malign the image of police departmental would largely depend upon the outcome of criminal case.
Until and unless the charges are proved, it may be difficult for the department to hold the petitioner guilty of the charges.

7. However, since now the matter is engaging attention of the disciplinary authority of the police, it is hereby provided that the petitioner will move an application for staying the proceedings of the departmental proceedings in light of the charges that are involved and it is provided that in the event any such application is moved by the petitioner seeking stay of the departmental proceedings,
the disciplinary authority shall look into and consider the same and shall pass appropriate orders within a period of thirty days from the date of production of certified copy of this order and in any case, before proceeding further in the matter of departmental inquiry.
8.
Thus, this petition stands disposed of.
